page: Microsoft Azure E64bds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by an Intel processor alongside 512.0 GB of system memory. This architecture establishes an 8.0 GB per-vCPU memory allocation ratio, aligning with workloads that require significant memory footprints without adding disproportionate compute cores. The instance does not include dedicated graphics processing units.

Storage configuration includes 3780 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity bundled directly with the instance. Additionally, the instance features enhanced block storage performance capabilities and support for premium storage tiers. Network provisioning does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring supplementary routing or address allocation for external network access.

From a hardware efficiency standpoint, the consolidation of dense memory capacity and large local NVMe storage reduces the requirement to provision external disk arrays for transient high-throughput data operations. Tradeoffs include the lack of hardware acceleration hardware and base IPv4 connectivity. The instance is tailored for enterprise relational database engines, in-memory caching solutions, large-scale extract-transform-load (ETL) processing, and analytical data workloads.
